architectureAxes._rule: Three independent architecture axes. Conflating them is an analysis error that has already been made once in this onboarding and corrected. Everything in `matrix` below is axis 1 and nothing else.

targetCluster.meaning: The architecture RHCOS runs on across control-plane and compute nodes, emitted into install-config and the mirror payload.

exportBinary.meaning: The architecture of the openshift-install / oc / oc-mirror binaries the operator downloads or receives in the export bundle.
exportBinary.governedBy: ReviewStep.jsx download selector and ocMirrorRuntime.js. NOT governed by this file.
exportBinary.standingRule: Do NOT infer export/download tool-binary availability from cluster-node support text. Red Hat publishes openshift-install-rhel9-arm64.tar.gz for 4.20.40, 4.21.35 and 4.22.16; the arm64 FIPS installer artifact was downloaded, SHA256-verified against the mirror's own checksum file, and confirmed to extract an ELF 64-bit LSB ARM aarch64 binary named openshift-install-fips. The "Linux ARM64 (RHEL 9 FIPS)" export option is therefore CORRECT and is not a defect. Regression coverage: frontend/tests/fips-installer-architectures.test.jsx.

runtimeHost.meaning: The architecture OpenShift Airgap Architect itself runs on.
runtimeHost.governedBy: backend/Containerfile. NOT governed by this file.

dispositions.supported: Same-minor Red Hat documentation documents this architecture for this platform and install method. Offered.
dispositions.locked: Same-minor Red Hat documentation documents this architecture as unavailable or restricted for this cell. Not offered, and the reason is shown.
dispositions.hidden: The platform does not offer this architecture at all, so the choice is not applicable and is not presented.
dispositions.unknown: No same-minor evidence was found either way, or two same-minor sources point different ways without resolving the combination. FAIL CLOSED: not offered. This is the DOC-156 'OPEN' state, recorded rather than filled in from another minor's data.

ppc64le.summary: Not offered: ppc64le agent-based installation is IBM Power installation — a separate platform Architect does not model.
ppc64le.reason: Resolved: ppc64le agent-based installation is IBM Power installation, not bare-metal installation. The OCP 4.21 Agent-based Installer book lists ppc64le in its installer-wide supported-architectures table, but that table is not split by platform, and the book handles IBM Power through dedicated procedures — for s390x it documents adding IBM Z agents with z/VM, RHEL KVM or LPAR and restricts ISO boot to RHEL KVM, with PXE-only for z/VM and LPAR. Installing on IBM Power is a separate platform with its own book, out of Architect's modelled scenario set, and the Installing on bare metal book documents amd64 and arm64 as the valid install-config architectures for THIS platform. ppc64le is therefore not applicable to the bare-metal agent scenario and is not presented.

For installations with z/VM and Logical Partition (LPAR), only PXE boot is supported. [The book carries dedicated "Adding IBM Z agents" procedures for z/VM, RHEL KVM and LPAR.]

aarch64.reason: Resolved against the OCP 4.21 Installing on Azure book: the 64-bit ARM material (tested ARM instance types) is generic and carries NO region qualification, while the "Supported Azure Government regions" section enumerates usgovtexas and usgovvirginia and says nothing about CPU architecture. Checked directly: every occurrence of the government-region term in that book was examined and NONE has an ARM or arm64 token within 700 characters, at this minor. Architect models Azure Government specifically, commercial-region support is not automatically government-region support, and under the documentation-veto rule absence of documentation never becomes supported — so 64-bit ARM is NOT presented for this scenario. Note: aarch64 is NOT among the architectures Red Hat states are FIPS-validated for cluster nodes at this minor. That is a cluster-node statement and says nothing about which client binaries Red Hat publishes.
